title: Russians Are Buying Fewer Clothes and Paying More for Them
subtitle: Between January and May the number of clothing and footwear items bought fell by 10% to 15%, while spending rose 5% to 7% on higher prices.

source.name: Russian clothing and footwear retail data reported by Kommersant

data.label: Items bought
data.annotation: Reported decline of 10% to 15% in units purchased.

data.label: Spending
data.annotation: Reported growth of 5% to 7%, driven entirely by price.

data.label: Premium prices
data.annotation: Prices in the premium segment rose 10% to 20%.

note: Midpoints of the reported ranges are plotted; the ranges themselves appear in the annotations.

supportingFacts.label: A wardrobe that shrinks while the bill grows is the household-level signature of price-driven retail growth.
The steepest price increases are in the premium segment, where the least price-sensitive buyers sit.

metadata.keyFinding: Clothing volumes fell while spending rose, with premium prices up as much as 20%.
